m1122.label: USCIS: Preparing for the naturalization test, M-1122 (PDF)

items.why: The filing date decides the civics test: before October 20, 2025 is the 2008 test; on or after is the 2025 test. Your interview date does not change this.
Age and residence rules (50/20, 55/15, 65/20) and disability exceptions have conditions. OathSteps can’t decide if they apply to you.
Some answers change after elections or depend on where you live. Check official websites close to your interview.
Ten minutes most days is easier to keep than long sessions. Set study reminders and quiet hours that fit your day.
Remembering on your own is closer to the interview than choosing from options.
Coming back after a gap checks that an answer has stayed with you.
Mocks help you get used to the format. Use the results to choose what to review.
Reading and writing are separate tests: one correct sentence out of up to three tries for each.
Read your copy of your application and make sure you understand each question. Answer with your own true information.
A qualified immigration attorney or a DOJ-accredited representative can advise on your case.
Your notice is the authority for your appointment. Follow what it says.
Use your notice and official guidance. Document needs differ from person to person.
Check the location ahead of time and any instructions about accommodations.
Arrive on time with your notice and documents. It’s okay to ask the officer to repeat a question.
Add the result to your journey so your plan matches what comes next.
A failed portion is usually retested 60 to 90 days after the first interview. Your notice gives the exact instructions.
Approval and taking the oath are separate steps. You become a citizen at the oath ceremony.
When you’re done, you can export or delete your OathSteps data in Settings.
